The "unit no longer working" suggests a malfunction, but the burn is the key event; the closest example case, also a thigh burn, was labeled improper procedure.

Inappropriate/Inadequate Shock/Stimulation is the best fit. The patient reports a vibrating sensation on the left side of the implant and says increasing the stimulation did not relieve bladder pressure, with baseline symptoms returning. Both point to stimulation that is felt inappropriately and does not work adequately. The implant protruding "like a bubble" under the skin was explained by the doctor as due to the patient being thin, so it is not treated as the main device problem.
